repository.description: Allowlisted demo repository. This frontend does not clone or scan it.

findings.title: Untrusted path reaches archive extraction
findings.safeSummary: A file-processing path can be steered outside its intended folder by a crafted name.
findings.remediationSummary: Resolve the final path and reject anything outside an allowlisted directory. Cover that rule with a regression test.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: If a name from outside the program is joined onto a folder, the program may open a file it was never meant to touch.
findings.learningGoal: Keep file access inside an allowlisted directory.
findings.hint1: Find the function that builds a filesystem path from request data.
findings.hint2: Check whether the path is compared to the archive root after it is resolved.
findings.hint3: Resolve the path, reject anything outside the allowlisted root, and add a regression test for names that try to leave it.
findings.mentorExplain: The fix works because the program decides from the final location, not the raw text of the name. A name can look harmless and still point somewhere else once the path is interpreted.
findings.testCheck: The regression test uses a safe fixture name and asserts the extractor refuses to leave the archive root. It does not demonstrate an attack.
fixAcceptanceCriteria: Resolved paths stay inside the allowlisted archive root
A regression test covers a name that tries to leave that root

findings.title: Request data is concatenated into a database query
findings.safeSummary: Untrusted input can become part of a database query string instead of a bound value.
findings.remediationSummary: Use a parameterized query and add a regression test that passes user text only as a bound parameter.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: Text from a request is being stitched into the query itself, so the database may treat that text as instructions.
findings.hint1: Find the code that constructs the query.
findings.hint2: Look at how request parameters are inserted into that query.
findings.hint3: Replace concatenation with bound parameters, and assert the test still finds the intended record.
findings.mentorExplain: Bound parameters keep the data separate from the query structure. The database can still search for the text, but it will not treat that text as part of the statement.
findings.testCheck: The test sends ordinary search text and checks that the query uses a placeholder with a bound value. It does not include a live exploit string.
fixAcceptanceCriteria: No untrusted string is concatenated into the query text

findings.title: Record route skips an authorization check
findings.safeSummary: A route can return another person's record without checking that the caller is allowed to see it.
findings.remediationSummary: Authorize the caller against the record owner before returning data, and test both an allowed and a denied caller.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: Being signed in is not the same as being allowed to open every record. This route never asks who the record belongs to.
findings.hint1: Find the handler that loads a record by id.
findings.hint2: See whether it compares the caller to the record owner or an allowed role.
findings.hint3: Add that check before the response, and cover an allowed caller and a denied caller in tests.
findings.mentorExplain: Authentication proves who is calling. Authorization decides whether that caller may see this record. Both have to succeed before the data is returned.
findings.testCheck: The test uses two fixture users. One owns the record and receives it. The other is denied. No private data is shown in the quest.
fixAcceptanceCriteria: The handler checks authorization before returning the record
Tests cover one allowed caller and one denied caller
